`Nat.ascFactorial` did not exist before this lane; it was one of the definitions named as blocking the open fact `F:ml430-nat-factorial-dvd-ascfactorial-44a4e641` (and, historically, the now-closed `F:ml430-nat-ascfactorial-zero-fd183202`/`F:ml430-nat-one-ascfactorial-8bacb017`/`F:ml430-nat-zero-ascfactorial-af4fcdca`, which were separately settled by the autogenesis statement-reflexivity system over a distinct synthetic construction, not this kernel's `Nat.ascFactorial`). This fact does NOT flip any `F:ml430-nat-*ascfactorial*` mirror fact by hand -- this kernel's `Nat.ascFactorial` is our own construction (structural recursion via `define_binary`, mirroring Mathlib's own equations exactly, but proved independently), not an import of Mathlib's proof, so claiming their statements verbatim would be the checker-that-cannot-fail defect this repository explicitly guards against.

The existence of the DEFINITION `Nat.ascFactorial` is entailed by this row rather than separately checked: the statement mentions `AxNat.ascFactorial`, and `Kernel::add_declaration` cannot admit a type naming a constant the environment does not contain.
